$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema path for editor validation.

scope.description: Optional Vercel team slug passed as `--scope` (or overridden by VERCEL_SCOPE env var). Leave empty ("") to use the default team from `vercel login`.

boardName.description: Optional named board within the Vercel team (`--name`, or VERCEL_BOARD_NAME env var). Leave empty ("") to use the team's default board.

inboxChannel.description: Board channel where humans post raw requests for the Lead agent to triage (without leading "#").

projectChannelPrefix.description: Channel path prefix for project task queues (e.g. "projects/" matches `#projects/<slug>`). Trailing slash is normalized automatically.

humanHandle.description: Human operator mention handle injected into Lead and Worker prompts for escalations (e.g. "@alice").

viewerPort.description: Localhost port for `board inspect` (from @vercel/board) on the main machine.

viewerUrl.description: Client-facing URL (e.g. Tailscale Caddy reverse proxy) where humans and Sheprd open the Board Inspector UI.

leaseDuration.description: Vercel Board task claim lease duration ("30s" to "1h", default "15m"). The deterministic dispatcher renews active leases automatically.

leaseRenewIntervalSeconds.description: How often (in seconds) the dispatcher renews active task leases. Must be shorter than `leaseDuration`.

board.description: Vercel Board connection, channel conventions, UI port, and lease settings.

machine.description: Key in `machines` where the Lead agent and Board Inspector UI run (e.g. `main-machine`).

boardProfile.description: Vercel Board profile name (`BOARD_PROFILE`) used by the Lead agent.

model.description: Claude CLI model or alias for the Lead agent (default "opus").

effort.description: Reasoning effort passed to the coding agent CLI (--effort). Use "" to omit the flag and rely on the CLI default.

permissionMode.description: Permission/approval policy for autonomous agents. Recommended: "auto" (maps to `--permission-mode auto` for claude and `--mode auto` for agy). "bypassPermissions" maps to `--dangerously-skip-permissions` on agy.

workspaceDir.description: Directory on the main machine where `apply-main` writes rendered `CLAUDE.md` and symlinks `projects.json`.

lead.description: Configuration for the persistent Lead triage agent on the main machine.

defaultAgent.description: Default agent profile key from `agents` used when a task does not specify an `agent=<name>` label (default "claude").

agents.description: Map of worker agent profile keys to CLI settings. Tasks can target any key here with `--label agent=<key>` (e.g. `agent=claude`, `agent=agy`).

kind.description: Herdr agent kind & CLI binary name passed to `herdr agent start --kind <kind>` (e.g. "claude", "agy", "codex", "opencode").

model.description: Model name or alias passed via `--model` (e.g. "opus" for claude). Leave empty ("") to omit `--model` and use the CLI's own default model (recommended for `agy`).

effort.description: Reasoning effort passed to the coding agent CLI (--effort). Use "" to omit the flag and rely on the CLI default.

permissionMode.description: Permission/approval policy for autonomous agents. Recommended: "auto" (maps to `--permission-mode auto` for claude and `--mode auto` for agy). "bypassPermissions" maps to `--dangerously-skip-permissions` on agy.

extraArgs.description: Additional raw CLI flags appended after `--` when launching this agent in Herdr.

additionalProperties.description: Configuration profile for a selectable worker agent CLI, routed via task label `agent=<profileKey>`.

useWorktree.description: Default workspace isolation mode. `false` spawns plain Herdr tabs in existing repo checkouts (guarded by a per-repo lock); `true` creates a Git worktree per task via `herdr worktree create`.

closeTabOnComplete.description: When true, automatically closes a worker's Herdr tab (or removes its temporary worktree) once the Board task becomes `completed` or `canceled`, keeping Sheprd clean.

keepTabOnBlockedOrFailed.description: When true, leaves `blocked` or `failed` worker tabs open in Sheprd renamed with `[BLOCKED]` or `[FAILED]` for human inspection.

maxParkedTabs.description: Maximum number of parked `[BLOCKED]`/`[FAILED]` tabs allowed before the dispatcher pauses claiming new tasks. Set 0 for unlimited.

pollIntervalSeconds.description: Seconds between dispatcher reconciliation and task-discovery ticks.

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: Seconds a worker agent may sit idle while its task is still `claimed` before the dispatcher sends a completion/block reminder (and parks it if still idle after a second window).

claimWaitSeconds.description: Reserved wait window in seconds for blocking claim operations.

workerDefaults.description: Default behavior and selectable agent CLI profiles for ephemeral task workers.

role.description: Host role in the swarm: "main" runs the Board Inspector UI and Lead agent; "worker" runs the Worker Dispatcher daemon; "both" runs both on one machine.

os.description: Host operating system ("linux" uses systemd --user services; "macos" uses launchd LaunchAgents). Automatically adds an `os=<os>` routing label.

hostname.description: Actual network/Tailscale hostname used to auto-identify this host and populate `board inspect --allow-host` when `allowedHosts` is omitted.

allowedHosts.description: Hostnames and host:port pairs passed to `board inspect --allow-host` on the main machine when served behind a reverse proxy (e.g. ["main-machine", "main-machine:4748"]).

herdrTarget.description: Herdr target for this dispatcher. Recommended: "local" (talks directly to the local `herdr server` socket). Can also be a saved `herdr machine list` label.

maxWorkers.description: Maximum concurrent ephemeral worker sessions this machine will claim and run (0 disables claiming, e.g. on a dedicated main machine).

labels.description: Additional routing labels matched against task labels. `machine=<key>` and `os=<os>` are added automatically.

items.description: Routing label in "key=value" format used to match Vercel Board task labels.

additionalProperties.description: Configuration for a single physical or virtual machine in the swarm.

machines.description: Map of logical machine keys (e.g. `main-machine`, `worker-machine`, or your real hostnames) to their OS, role, capacity, and labels.
